target: GazeMotive (demonstration system) / gaze-to-feedback architecture (TERM)
note: Names and describes the working Windows-desktop application: a Tobii eye tracker plus self-report feed previously-built logistic regression models, whose motivational-state inferences drive a pedagogical agent's real-time personalised text/picture feedback (FE, p.544-547).

target: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
note: The paper's real organizing construct: the system exists to detect and remediate low motivation/engagement and sustain 'motivation-enhanced learning experience and better learning performance'; 'motivation and engagement' are named together as the target outcome (FE, p.544-546).

target: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
note: Treated only indirectly, via two gaze-detected proxies rather than the paper's own vocabulary: a 'negative reading experience' flagged during a learning page, and a user detected as 'having not put enough effort' during a quiz (FE, p.546-547, Fig.2) (P/anticipatory-application for the construct mapping).

target: situational vs. trait/state boredom
note: Not treated as boredom, but the motivation model draws a parallel stability split: Self-Efficacy/Attitudes Toward School are trait-like and assessed once via self-report, while Confirmed Fit/Reading Experience vary dynamically and are assessed continuously from gaze -- a motivation-domain analogue, not a boredom-domain claim (FE, p.546).

target: gaze variance / fixation dispersion
note: Tobii Eye Tracker 4C; AOI-based gaze features including fixation number, computed per learning-material page; accuracy figure (up to 81.3%) borrowed from the cited prior study ref [5], no new figure reported here (FE, p.545-546).

target: pupil dilation / pupillometry
note: Average pupil diameter, cited from ref [5]'s prior experiment as one of two gaze features (with fixation number) carrying significant motivation-prediction weight (FE, p.545-546).

target: self-report / survey scale
note: Self-input data collected at session start for stable intrinsic-motivation factors (Attitudes Toward School, Self-Efficacy), plus the multi-item questionnaire study underlying the original motivation model (refs [1],[2]) (FE, p.545-546).

target: ML classification
note: Previously-built logistic regression models (from ref [5]) mapping gaze features to motivational-factor scores; GazeMotive states it 'improved the prediction models by including only the gaze features that have significant prediction power,' reporting no new accuracy figure (FE, p.545-546).

target: behavioral (RT / errors / performance-monitoring)
note: Quiz-answer correctness combined with gaze-detected effort level to trigger quiz-stage personalised feedback (FE, p.546-547, Fig.2b).

target: flow / engagement (motivation broadly) <- ML classification (logistic regression on gaze features)
note: The paper's own internal construct-measure pairing: motivational-factor states (feeding the engagement-sustaining feedback loop) are inferred from gaze features via the reused logistic regression models (FE, p.545-546).

target: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness (negative reading experience / insufficient effort) <- gaze variance/fixation dispersion + pupil dilation
note: The paper's own internal construct-measure pairing: the two named feedback triggers are detected directly from gaze features (fixation, pupil diameter) rather than from self-report (FE, p.546-547, Fig.2).

target: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
note: Concrete instantiation via Fig.2's two screenshots: (a) a learning-page feedback message triggered by gaze-detected 'negative reading experience'; (b) a quiz-stage feedback message triggered by an incorrect answer co-occurring with gaze-detected low effort (FE, p.546-547).
